paper.citation: Dimitriadis, T., Dümbgen, L., Henzi, A., Puke, M. and Ziegel, J. (2023). Honest calibration assessment for binary outcome predictions. Biometrika, 110(3), 663–680. DOI: 10.1093/biomet/asac068.
paper.venue: Biometrika (formal publication, 2023); arXiv preprint v2 is the checked DGP version
paper.source_locator: DGP source actually checked in arXiv:2203.04065v2 (2022-11-02), PDF p.8, Section 5, item 1 (Monomial); X~U[0,1] and Y~Bernoulli{p_s(X)} on the same page. The paper gives replication URL https://github.com/marius-cp/replication_DDHPZ22 but no fixed code commit. Formal Biometrika DGP differences were not checked.

mechanism.name: Monomial binary regression functions from Dimitriadis et al. (2023)

sampling.dependence: iid across observations; no cluster, panel, network, or within-unit dependence

assumptions: Independent and identically distributed individual observations (X_i,Y_i).
X has the source distribution Uniform[0,1] and the fixed query x*=0.5 lies in its support interior.
Given X=x, Y is Bernoulli with success probability p_s(x)=x^(1-s); s<1 ensures the declared source scenarios are defined.
For every declared scenario s<=0.9, p_s is nondecreasing on [0,1], matching the monotonicity condition used for the source simultaneous-band method.
The scalar truth is evaluated under the known DGP; no causal exchangeability, treatment, mediator, or interference assumption is relevant.

properties.notes: The only covariate is X, so total and effective dimensions are both one. There are no interaction terms. The regression curve is the power function x^(1-s), nonlinear for s>0 and linear at the nested s=0 diagonal case; the binary outcome link is Bernoulli with this conditional probability. s=0 is retained as the source monomial endpoint and should be deduplicated against any separately registered s_shape/kink/wave s=0 scenario.

estimand.name: m_s(x*) = E[Y | X=x*] = p_s(x*)
estimand.definition: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0,0.1,...,0.9}; with p_s(x)=x^(1-s), the target is p_s(0.5). This is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.

truth.expression: Noncausal nonparametric regression function at the fixed query x*=0.5 for a selected source scenario s in {0,0.1,...,0.9}; with p_s(x)=x^(1-s), the target is p_s(0.5). This is a conditional Bernoulli probability, not an intervention effect or a prediction interval.
truth.derivation: Closed-form substitution p_s(0.5)=0.5^(1-s), independently checked with exp((1-s)*log(0.5)); default s=0.5 equals sqrt(0.5).

adaptations: Register s=0,0.1,...,0.9 as named scenarios and use s=0.5 as the default scenario; these are source parameter settings, not new mechanism families.
Expose the scalar NRI target p_s(0.5)=E[Y|X=0.5] required by the collection interface. The source studies simultaneous confidence bands over x, not this scalar truth hook.
Run the collection smoke check instead of the source's 1000-replication coverage experiment; no confidence band, bootstrap, or coverage result is claimed.
